lessons.0.slides.1.title: Côte de Nuits
lessons.0.slides.1.content: The Côte de Nuits is Burgundy's most celebrated red wine region, stretching roughly 20 km south of Dijon to Corgoloin. It produces the world's most expensive and most elegant Pinot Noir.
lessons.0.slides.2.title: Map of the Nine Key Villages
lessons.0.slides.2.description: Click the buttons to explore each village's location and boundaries
lessons.0.slides.3.title: 🍷 What Makes the Côte de Nuits Special
lessons.0.slides.3.points.0: 24 Grand Crus, 23 of which produce red wine
lessons.0.slides.3.points.1: Ideal terroir conditions for Pinot Noir
lessons.0.slides.3.points.2: East- and south-east-facing slopes at 250–300 m elevation
lessons.0.slides.3.points.3: Predominantly limestone soils with excellent drainage
lessons.0.slides.3.points.4: Wines are structured, firm in tannin, with extraordinary ageing potential
lessons.0.slides.4.title: 📍 Nine Key Villages (North to South)
lessons.0.slides.4.points.0: Marsannay — the only village permitted to produce all three colours
lessons.0.slides.4.points.5: Vougeot — famous for the Clos de Vougeot Grand Cru
lessons.0.slides.4.points.8: Nuits-Saint-Georges — no Grand Crus but many outstanding Premiers Crus
lessons.0.slides.5.title: Nine Villages Style Chart (Côte de Nuits Axis)
lessons.0.slides.6.title: Côte de Nuits vs. Côte de Beaune Reds
lessons.0.slides.6.content: The two regions produce strikingly different styles of Pinot Noir, each with its own merits. The Côte de Nuits is known for powerful structure; the Côte de Beaune for elegance and finesse.
lessons.0.slides.7.title: Why Is the Côte de Nuits So Exceptional?
lessons.0.slides.7.content: The uniqueness of the Côte de Nuits stems from a perfect convergence of terroir: morning sunlight from east-facing slopes, mineral character from limestone soils, cool nights from a continental climate that preserve acidity, and centuries of meticulous parcel mapping by monks and growers.
lessons.0.slides.8.title: 🧠 Côte de Nuits Overview Quiz
lessons.1.title: Gevrey-Chambertin Village
lessons.1.slides.0.title: Gevrey-Chambertin
lessons.1.slides.0.subtitle: Lesson 2 - 18 min
lessons.1.slides.0.description: Explore the Côte de Nuits' largest village — a kingdom of wine with nine Grand Crus
lessons.1.slides.1.title: Gevrey-Chambertin
lessons.1.slides.1.content: This is the largest village in the Côte de Nuits, with 9 Grand Crus and over 400 hectares of vineyards. Chambertin — Napoleon's favourite wine — is found here. The reds are renowned for power, concentration, and the need for long ageing.
lessons.1.slides.2.title: Gevrey-Chambertin Map
lessons.1.slides.2.description: Click the buttons to explore the village-level appellation and the nine Grand Crus
lessons.1.slides.3.title: 👑 The Nine Grand Crus
lessons.1.slides.3.points.1: Chambertin-Clos de Bèze — may be labelled as Chambertin
lessons.1.slides.3.points.7: Mazoyères-Chambertin — may be labelled as Charmes
lessons.1.slides.4.title: 🍇 Gevrey-Chambertin Style
lessons.1.slides.4.points.1: Aromas: black cherry, blackberry, liquorice, animal leather
lessons.1.slides.4.points.2: Palate: powerful and forceful, firm tannins
lessons.1.slides.4.points.4: Ageing: needs 10–30 years to fully open up
lessons.1.slides.5.title: 🏰 Key Producers
lessons.1.slides.6.title: Tasting & Serving Advice
lessons.1.slides.6.content: Gevrey-Chambertin needs time. Young wines have tight tannins and closed fruit. Age for at least 10 years, decant in a large Burgundy glass for 1–2 hours, and serve at 16–18°C.
lessons.1.slides.7.title: 🧠 Gevrey-Chambertin Quiz
lessons.2.title: Chambolle-Musigny and Morey-Saint-Denis
lessons.2.slides.0.title: Chambolle-Musigny & Morey-Saint-Denis
lessons.2.slides.0.subtitle: Lesson 3 - 18 min
lessons.2.slides.0.description: Explore the most elegant and most underrated villages of the Côte de Nuits
lessons.2.slides.1.title: Chambolle-Musigny
lessons.2.slides.1.content: If Gevrey-Chambertin represents the power of the Côte de Nuits, Chambolle-Musigny is the embodiment of elegance. Its wines are prized for silky texture, delicate tannins, and floral aromatics — the most feminine style in the Côte de Nuits.
lessons.2.slides.2.title: Chambolle-Musigny Map
lessons.2.slides.2.description: Click the buttons to explore village-level and Grand Cru vineyards
lessons.2.slides.3.title: 💎 Chambolle-Musigny Grand Crus
lessons.2.slides.3.points.0: Musigny — 10.9 ha, the most elegant in the Côte de Nuits
lessons.2.slides.3.points.2: Musigny Blanc — an extraordinarily rare Grand Cru white wine
lessons.2.slides.4.title: 🌹 Chambolle-Musigny Style
lessons.2.slides.4.points.1: Aromas: violet, rose, red berries, spice
lessons.2.slides.4.points.5: Character: the most feminine red wine in the Côte de Nuits
lessons.2.slides.5.title: Morey-Saint-Denis
lessons.2.slides.5.content: Sandwiched between Gevrey-Chambertin and Chambolle-Musigny, Morey-Saint-Denis is often overlooked, yet it harbours 5 Grand Crus. Its style sits between those of its neighbours, combining power and elegance.
lessons.2.slides.6.title: Morey-Saint-Denis Map
lessons.2.slides.6.description: Click the buttons to explore village-level and the five Grand Crus
lessons.2.slides.7.title: 👑 Morey-Saint-Denis Grand Crus
lessons.2.slides.7.points.0: Clos de la Roche — the largest at 16.9 ha
lessons.2.slides.7.points.3: Clos de Tart — 7.5 ha, single ownership
lessons.2.slides.7.points.4: Bonnes-Mares — a portion lies within this village
lessons.2.slides.8.title: Three-Village Comparison
lessons.2.slides.9.title: What Makes Morey-Saint-Denis Unique?
lessons.2.slides.9.content: Morey-Saint-Denis strikes a perfect balance between its neighbours — it has Gevrey's structure and depth while retaining Chambolle's elegance and finesse. This balance makes it an outstanding value proposition.
lessons.2.slides.10.title: 🧠 Chambolle-Musigny & Morey-Saint-Denis Quiz
lessons.3.title: Vosne-Romanée: The Grand Cru Paradise
lessons.3.slides.0.title: Vosne-Romanée
lessons.3.slides.0.subtitle: Lesson 4 - 20 min
lessons.3.slides.0.description: Discover the legendary village with 8 Grand Crus, including the world's most expensive wine
lessons.3.slides.1.title: Vosne-Romanée
lessons.3.slides.1.content: This is the heart of Burgundy and a pilgrimage site for wine lovers the world over. This small village holds 8 Grand Crus, including the legendary Romanée-Conti — where every bottle commands an astronomical price.
lessons.3.slides.2.title: Vosne-Romanée Map
lessons.3.slides.2.description: Click the buttons to explore village-level and the eight Grand Crus
lessons.3.slides.3.title: 👑 The Eight Grand Crus
lessons.3.slides.3.points.0: Romanée-Conti — 1.8 ha, the world's most expensive wine
lessons.3.slides.3.points.1: La Tâche — 6.1 ha, monopole of DRC
lessons.3.slides.3.points.2: La Romanée — 0.85 ha, the smallest Grand Cru
lessons.3.slides.4.title: Romanée-Conti
lessons.3.slides.4.content: The world's most expensive and most sought-after wine. Just 1.8 hectares, producing around 450 cases (5,400 bottles) per year. Purchased by the Prince de Conti in 1760, it is now the exclusive monopole of Domaine de la Romanée-Conti (DRC). A great vintage bottle can sell for over USD 100,000.
lessons.3.slides.5.title: 🍷 Vosne-Romanée Style
lessons.3.slides.5.points.0: A perfect balance of power and elegance
lessons.3.slides.5.points.1: Exceptionally complex aromas: rose, violet, cherry, spice, truffle
lessons.3.slides.5.points.5: Each Grand Cru expresses a distinct and unmistakable personality
lessons.3.slides.6.title: 🏰 Legendary Domaines
lessons.3.slides.7.title: Why Are the Prices So High?
lessons.3.slides.7.content: Vosne-Romanée's premium stems from: 1) Tiny production — RC is just 1.8 ha  2) Unique, irreproducible terroir  3) Historical legend and prestige  4) Global demand from wealthy collectors  5) Genuinely transcendent quality.
lessons.3.slides.8.title: 💡 Investment & Collecting Advice
lessons.3.slides.8.points.0: RC: requires a very large budget — for the most serious collectors
lessons.3.slides.8.points.1: La Tâche: relatively more accessible, high investment value
lessons.3.slides.8.points.2: Richebourg: a better-value alternative among the DRC lineup
lessons.3.slides.8.points.3: Village wines: top producers' village-level wines are also worth cellaring
lessons.3.slides.8.points.4: Ageing potential: great vintages can develop over 30–50 years
lessons.3.slides.8.points.5: Storage: requires a temperature- and humidity-controlled cellar (12–14°C)
lessons.3.slides.9.title: 🧠 Vosne-Romanée Quiz
lessons.4.title: Nuits-Saint-Georges and Other Villages
lessons.4.slides.0.title: Nuits-Saint-Georges & Other Villages
lessons.4.slides.0.subtitle: Lesson 5 - 14 min
lessons.4.slides.0.description: Explore the important villages of the southern Côte de Nuits and their value offerings
lessons.4.slides.1.title: Nuits-Saint-Georges
lessons.4.slides.1.content: The southernmost important village of the Côte de Nuits, and the source of its name. Although it has no Grand Crus, Nuits-Saint-Georges boasts 41 Premiers Crus covering 143 hectares. Its reds are known for power and longevity.
lessons.4.slides.2.title: Value Villages of the Côte de Nuits — Map
lessons.4.slides.2.description: Click the buttons to locate Nuits-Saint-Georges, Marsannay, and Fixin
lessons.4.slides.3.title: 🍷 Nuits-Saint-Georges Character
lessons.4.slides.3.points.0: No Grand Crus, but 41 outstanding Premiers Crus
lessons.4.slides.3.points.1: Style: powerful and robust, firm tannins
lessons.4.slides.3.points.2: Aromas: dark fruit, animal leather, truffle
lessons.4.slides.3.points.4: Value: far more approachable in price than Grand Crus
lessons.4.slides.3.points.5: Notable Premiers Crus: Les Saint-Georges, Les Vaucrains, Les Cailles
lessons.4.slides.4.title: Marsannay
lessons.4.slides.4.content: The northernmost village of the Côte de Nuits, elevated to village AOC status in 2009. It is the only village in the Côte de Nuits legally permitted to produce red, white, and rosé — and its rosé is particularly celebrated.
lessons.4.slides.5.title: 🌸 Marsannay Rosé
lessons.4.slides.5.points.0: The only village in the Côte de Nuits permitted to produce rosé
lessons.4.slides.5.points.2: Colour: pale pink to onion-skin hues
lessons.4.slides.5.points.4: Palate: fresh, lively, with a mineral edge
lessons.4.slides.5.points.5: Perfect for summer and Asian cuisine pairings
lessons.4.slides.6.title: Fixin
lessons.4.slides.6.content: Immediately south of Gevrey-Chambertin, Fixin shares a similar style but at a far more accessible price. Its reds are powerful and require ageing — making them an outstanding value choice.
lessons.4.slides.7.title: 💎 Value Village Recommendations
lessons.4.slides.7.points.0: Fixin — similar to Gevrey at a reasonable price
lessons.4.slides.7.points.2: Nuits-Saint-Georges village — Premiers Crus are pricey but village wines are approachable
lessons.4.slides.7.points.3: Côte de Nuits-Villages — regional level but often excellent quality
lessons.4.slides.7.points.4: Tip: seek out village-level wines from top producers
lessons.4.slides.8.title: Côte de Nuits — Summary
lessons.4.slides.8.content: The Côte de Nuits is the spiritual home of Pinot Noir. From the power of Gevrey-Chambertin to the elegance of Chambolle-Musigny, from the legend of Romanée-Conti to the value of Fixin — here, every facet of Pinot Noir's potential is revealed.
